news.title: Sonia Bompastor on finding a way to win and praise for Potter
news.title_zh: 索尼娅·邦帕斯特 (Sonia Bompastor) 寻找获胜方法并对波特表示赞扬
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained how the Blues put together a 3-0 win over West Ham and described Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter as a 'starter' for the team. A clinical finish from Melvine Malard seven minutes from half-time saw us take the lead, while goals in the final ten minutes of the match from Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano completed a dominant display against the Hammers. This was our sixth consecutive clean sheet. Today's game was played at the end of a gruelling 11 days during which time we faced Austria Vienna and Arsenal at home before away matches against Lyon and West Ham. 'When you are Chelsea, you need to find different ways to win the games,' said Bompastor after the 3-0 victory. 'Today was about winning. We knew coming into this game that it was the last one in a really intense and condensed block: many fixtures, big games, and also a lot of travel. 'We weren’t as fresh as we would have liked to have been, but we found a way to win. We didn't concede much against this team, and we know they were probably looking to hurt us in transition. 'We knew coming into this game we had to be a little bit patient because we were going to face a team that would defend with a back five today, a low block, so the spaces were not always open. 'So we stayed strong; we scored a really important goal in the first half, we kept the clean sheet, and we were able to break them in the second half.' The Blues head coach introduced Lexi Potter at half-time in place of Sjoeke Nusken. The 20-year-old has impressed with some strong displays alongside Keira Walsh in midfield, so much so that Potter will now join up with the senior England side for the first time. Bompastor linked a more controlled second-half performance with Potter's introduction. She even went so far as to say that the Academy graduate had won a place among Chelsea's starters, before also praising Walsh's impact against West Ham. 'As you could see, when Lexi is playing for our team, she is really good right now,' she explained. 'She brings calmness; she brings quality on the ball. At the level she's performing right now, she's a starter for us. There is no doubt about that. 'We controlled the ball more in the second half, and the quality we had on the ball was better as well. With Lexi being on the pitch, it helps a lot. 'Keira is playing a little bit higher than probably last season. It helps us a lot in terms of creating opportunities. We know how good she is when she is at the edge of the box; even if the opposition knows what she’s going to do, her shot is so great that she’s able to score. 'And right now it's good to have a player who is confident and brings us the solution to scoring goals. That's really important.'
news.body_zh: 索尼娅·邦帕斯特 (Sonia Bompastor) 解释了蓝军如何 3-0 战胜西汉姆联队，并将切尔西学院毕业生莱克西·波特 (Lexi Potter) 描述为球队的“首发”。半场结束后 7 分钟，梅尔文·马拉德 (Melvine Malard) 的冷静射门让我们取得了领先，而凯拉·沃尔什 (Keira Walsh) 和麦卡·滨野 (Maika Hamano) 在比赛最后 10 分钟的进球完成了对铁锤队的统治性表现。这是我们连续第六次零失球。今天的比赛是在艰苦的 11 天之后进行的，这期间我们主场对阵奥地利维也纳和阿森纳，然后客场对阵里昂和西汉姆联。 “当你是切尔西队的时候，你需要找到不同的方式来赢得比赛，”邦帕斯特在3-0获胜后说道。 “今天是关于胜利的。我们知道，进入这场比赛后，这是一场真正紧张而紧凑的比赛中的最后一场：许多赛程、大型比赛，还有大量的旅行。 “我们并没有像我们希望的那样充满活力，但我们找到了获胜的方法。我们在对阵这支球队时并没有丢太多球，而且我们知道他们可能想在攻防转换中伤害我们。 “我们知道进入这场比赛我们必须有点耐心，因为今天我们将面对一支用五后卫防守的球队，一个低位防守，所以空间并不总是开放的。 “所以我们保持坚强；我们在上半场打进了一个非常重要的进球，我们保持了不失球，并在下半场打破了对手。”蓝军主教练在半场休息时用莱克西·波特代替了肖克·努斯肯。这位20岁的球员在中场与凯拉·沃尔什并肩作战时的出色表现给人留下了深刻的印象，以至于波特现在将首次与英格兰成年队联手。邦帕斯特将下半场更加受控的表现与波特的上场联系起来。她甚至说这位青训毕业生已经在切尔西的首发中赢得了一席之地，然后还赞扬了沃尔什在对阵西汉姆联队的比赛中的表现。 “正如你所看到的，当莱克西为我们球队效力时，她现在真的很棒，”她解释道。 “她带来平静；她给球带来了质量。以她现在的表现来说，她是我们的先发球员。毫无疑问。 “下半场我们控球能力更强，控球质量也更好。有莱克西在场上，这很有帮助。 “凯拉的表现比上赛季可能要高一些。它在创造机会方面对我们有很大帮助。当她处于禁区边缘时，我们知道她有多出色；即使对手知道她要做什么，她的射门也非常出色，能够得分。 “现在拥有一名充满自信并为我们带来进球解决方案的球员是件好事。这真的很重要。

news.title: Match report: West Ham United 0-3 Chelsea Women
news.title_zh: 赛报：西汉姆联0-3切尔西女足
news.body_en: Goals from Melvine Malard, Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano sealed a valuable victory away to West Ham United on Sunday afternoon. Coming straight into today's clash with West Ham after Wednesday's tough battle against Lyon was always going to be a big ask for the Blues. It was therefore no surprise that it was tough to find a way through during the opening exchanges as we were unable to create any clear-cut chances. Our pressing paid off after 38 minutes, when Sjoeke Nusken pounced on some slack short passing from the Hammers in midfield, setting up Melvine Malard with her back to goal. The striker did not need to be asked twice to turn and finish, putting us ahead at the break with a fine strike. There was not much action at either end for long periods of the second half, but after some changes from Sonia Bompastor, we were able to extend our advantage. A trademark effort from Walsh from the edge of the penalty area was followed by a header from Maika Hamano, both goals created by Alyssa Thompson on the left. At the end of a gruelling period of fixtures, this was the best way to finish before the international break: a 3-0 victory and our sixth clean sheet in a row during a match where West Ham produced nothing in the final third of the pitch. Bompastor made just two alterations from our impressive 0-0 draw away at Lyon in midweek, switching Lexi Potter and Thompson for Sandy Baltimore and Hamano, the Japan international making her first start of the season. Erin Cuthbert made the matchday squad for the first time since being announced as Chelsea captain, having completed her recovery from an injury sustained whilst on international duty with Scotland during the summer. And the Blues started the game in Dagenham with typical intent. Ellie Carpenter stormed down the right wing and got her cross away, forcing the home side to clear their lines quickly. And when Walsh made a run down the channel and played a diagonal ball to Nusken in the box, the Chelsea number six couldn't quite keep her shot down as she slid in to meet the cross. Carpenter won a corner on the half-hour mark with a powerful half-volley, which ricocheted off a West Ham defender. But the Blues were struggling to make a real impact in the final third, with no shots on target to show for 64 per cent possession and 16 touches in the opposition box. Up until that point, striker Malard hadn't had much of a sniff on goal. Yet when she got a chance, she took it with a clinical finish to put us in front eight minutes before half-time. The opportunity came from a West Ham free-kick in the midfield area. Nusken, sensing a moment's hesitation, used the press to steal the ball from the opposition and strode forward, with the ball finding Malard. The number nine received it with her back to goal, but stood strong, turned and stroked her finish into the bottom corner. We headed in at the interval with the one-goal advantage, and the home side had failed to take a single shot on goal in the opening 45 minutes. Neither side was able to fashion a clear chance after the restart, but just after the hour mark the Blues came alive once more. Some neat interplay on the edge of the box between Wieke Kaptein, Malard and Walsh was only lacking the finish to make it 2-0. Bompastor then shuffled the pack in attack, bringing on Aggie Beever-Jones and Alyssa Thompson in place of Baltimore and goalscorer Malard. The fresh impetus saw us go close when Beever-Jones charged down the right flank, playing the ball square to Kaptein on the edge of the area. Walsh then took her trademark shot from range, crashing her attempt onto the right-hand post. A 1-0 victory wouldn't have done Chelsea's dominance justice, and after looking dangerous from the edge of the area all game, Walsh finally got her goal and added our second of the afternoon. Thompson jinked her way towards goal from the left-hand side before playing a short sideways pass for Kaptein. The Netherlands international quickly shifted the ball to Walsh, and the midfielder used her tried and tested technique to fire the ball into the bottom corner. The strike put the match beyond reasonable doubt against a side who had still not registered a single shot on goal. Our third of the afternoon came from another of Thompson's runs down the left. This time, the American took a shot, which was saved before Beever-Jones picked up the loose ball and steered it towards Hamano, who was able to head home at the far post. Substitute McCabe whipped in a corner right under the crossbar, with keeper Constance Picaud-Inconnu only just managing to tip it over. The final whistle blew with no shots and no touches in our box from the home side. A truly dominant performance to end this block of fixtures. The victory, along with Tottenham's defeat to London City Lionesses, means we move into top spot in the WSL, pending Manchester City's result with Arsenal later this afternoon. Our players will now head off to represent their respective national teams during the international break. We return to action with a home game against Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on 18 October. Chelsea:  Hampton, Carpenter, Bronze (c), Buchanan (McCabe 77), Buurman (Bjorn 86), Kaptein, Walsh, Nusken (Potter h-t), Baltimore (Thompson 65), Hamano, Malard (Beever-Jones 65)Unused substitutes: Peng, Cuthbert, Dragoni, James Scorers: Malard 38, Walsh 80, Hamano 87Booked: Kaptein 32 West Ham: Picaud-Inconnu, Codina, Siren, Belloumou, Kumagai, Zelem (c), Gago (Wandeler 69), Asseyi, Riesen (Endo 88), Cascarino, Puibel (Tennebo 81)Unused substitutes: Walsh, Dowsett, Wareing, Morgan, PeacockReferee: Sophie Dennington
news.body_zh: 周日下午，梅尔文·马拉德、凯拉·沃尔什和滨野麦卡的进球锁定了客场对阵西汉姆联队的宝贵胜利。在周三对阵里昂的艰苦战斗之后，直接进入今天与西汉姆联的比赛对蓝军来说总是一个很大的要求。因此，在开局交锋中很难找到出路也就不足为奇了，因为我们无法创造任何明确的机会。第 38 分钟后，我们的逼抢得到了回报，Sjoeke Nusken 接住了铁锤帮中场的短传，为梅尔文·马拉德 (Melvine Malard) 背身球门助攻。这名前锋不需要两次转身就完成射门，凭借一脚漂亮的射门让我们在中场休息时取得领先。下半场的很长一段时间里，双方都没有太多动作，但在索尼娅·邦帕斯托尔做出一些改变后，我们能够扩大我们的优势。沃尔什在禁区边缘打出标志性射门，随后滨野麦卡头球破门，这两粒进球均由左侧的阿丽莎·汤普森攻入。在经历了一段艰苦的比赛之后，这是国际比赛日之前最好的结束方式：我们以 3-0 取得胜利，并在西汉姆联队在最后三分之一的比赛中连续第六次不失球。周中我们客场0-0战平里昂的比赛中，邦帕斯特只做出了两次调整，用莱克西·波特和汤普森换下了桑迪·巴尔的摩和日本国脚滨野，这是她本赛季的首次首发。艾琳·库斯伯特 (Erin Cuthbert) 自被宣布担任切尔西队长以来首次入选比赛日阵容，她在夏季代表苏格兰国家队期间受伤，现已完全康复。蓝军在达格纳姆以典型的意图开始了比赛。埃莉·卡彭特从右翼猛冲过来，将她的传中球挡开，迫使主队迅速清理防线。当沃尔什沿着通道跑动并向禁区内的努斯肯打出斜线球时，这位切尔西六号球员在滑入接球时无法完全控制射门。卡彭特在半小时内凭借一记强力半凌空抽射赢得了角球，球被西汉姆联后卫击中。但蓝军在最后三分之一的比赛中难以发挥真正的作用，在对方禁区有 64% 的控球率和 16 次触球，没有射正。在那之前，前锋马拉德还没有对进球有太多的嗅觉。然而，当她有机会时，她以冷静的射门抓住了机会，在半场结束前八分钟让我们领先。机会来自西汉姆联中场的任意球。努斯肯察觉到了片刻的犹豫，利用压迫从对方手中抢断了球，大步向前，球传给了马拉德。九号球员背对球门接球，但她坚强地站了起来，转身将球射入球门底角。我们在中场休息时以一球优势头球破门，而主队在开场45分钟内一次都没能射正。比赛重新开始后，双方都未能创造出明显的机会，但就在一个小时之后，蓝军再次活跃起来。 Wieke Kaptein、Malard 和 Walsh 在禁区边缘巧妙的配合，只是缺少射门，将比分改写为 2-0。随后，邦帕斯特在进攻中重新调整了阵容，用阿吉·比弗-琼斯和阿丽莎·汤普森代替巴尔的摩和进球者马拉德。当比弗-琼斯从右翼冲锋，将球传给禁区边缘的卡普坦时，我们的新动力让我们逼近了比分。随后沃尔什进行了她标志性的远距离射门，击中了右侧门柱。 1-0 的胜利并不能体现切尔西的统治地位，整场比赛在禁区边缘看起来都很危险，沃尔什终于进球了，为我们打进了下午的第二粒进球。汤普森从左侧冲向球门，然后为卡普坦进行了一次短侧传球。荷兰国脚迅速将球传给沃尔什，沃尔什用她久经考验的技术将球射入底角。这一粒进球让这场比赛毫无疑问地战胜了一支还没有射门的球队。下午的第三个进球来自汤普森的另一次左路跑动。这一次，美国人射门，但在比弗-琼斯捡起球并将其引向滨野之前，射门被扑出，滨野在远门柱头球破门。 替补出场的麦凯布在横梁正下方开出角球，门将康斯坦斯·皮考德-因康努刚刚将球打翻。终场哨响了，主队没有射门，也没有触球。一场真正具有统治力的表现结束了这一系列的比赛。这场胜利，加上托特纳姆热刺队输给伦敦城狮队，意味着我们将跻身女超级联赛榜首，等待今天下午晚些时候曼城对阵阿森纳的结果。我们的球员现在将在国际比赛日期间代表各自的国家队出发。 10 月 18 日，我们将在斯坦福桥主场迎战托特纳姆热刺队。切尔西：汉普顿、卡彭特、青铜（c）、布坎南（麦凯布 77）、布尔曼（比约恩 86）、卡普坦、沃尔什、努斯肯（波特 h-t）、巴尔的摩（汤普森 65）、滨野、马拉德（比弗-琼斯 65）未上场替补：彭、库斯伯特、德拉戈尼、詹姆斯 进球者：马拉德 38、沃尔什80、滨野 87 黄牌：卡普坦 32 西汉姆联：皮科-因康努、科迪纳、塞伦、贝卢穆、熊谷、泽勒姆（中）、加戈（万德勒 69）、阿塞伊、里森（远藤 88）、卡斯卡里诺、普伊贝尔（天内博 81）未上场替补：沃尔什、多塞特、韦林、摩根、孔雀裁判：索菲·丹宁顿

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs West Ham United
news.title_zh: 确认切尔西女足对阵西汉姆联的阵容
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made two changes to her Chelsea side for our Women's Super League match against West Ham United this afternoon. After receiving medical treatment late in the game against Lyon, Hannah Hampton is fit and starts for the Blues in goal. The backline remains unchanged, but Lexi Potter and Alyssa Thompson are rested, with Sandy Baltimore returning to the starting XI and Maika Hamano making her first start of the campaign. Katie McCabe returns to the bench after suffering from illness in midweek, while Melvine Malard continues to lead the line up front. There is good news for Chelsea supporters as newly-named captain Erin Cuthbert is named in the squad for the first time this season after completing her recovery from injury. Chelsea: Hampton, Carpenter, Bronze (c), Buchanan, Buurman, Kaptein, Walsh, Nusken, Baltimore, Hamano, Malard Chelsea substitutes: Peng, Bjorn, McCabe, Potter, Cuthbert, Dragoni, James, Thompson, Beever-Jones
news.body_zh: 今天下午对阵西汉姆联队的女足超级联赛比赛中，索尼娅·邦帕斯特对她的切尔西队做出了两项调整。在对阵里昂的比赛后期接受治疗后，汉娜·汉普顿已经恢复健康，并开始为蓝军守门。后防线保持不变，但莱克西·波特和艾莉莎·汤普森得到了休息，桑迪·巴尔的摩重返首发阵容，而滨野麦卡则在本赛季首次首发。凯蒂·麦凯布 (Katie McCabe) 在周中患病后回到替补席，而梅尔文·马拉德 (Melvine Malard) 则继续领衔锋线。对于切尔西的支持者来说，这是个好消息，新任命的队长艾琳·库斯伯特在从伤病中恢复过来后，本赛季首次入选球队。切尔西：汉普顿、卡彭特、青铜（中）、布坎南、布尔曼、卡普坦、沃尔什、努斯肯、巴尔的摩、滨野、马拉德 切尔西替补：彭、比约恩、麦凯布、波特、库斯伯特、德拉戈尼、詹姆斯、汤普森、比弗-琼斯

news.title: 1996/97 remembered - part one: Chelsea’s seismic summer
news.title_zh: 纪念 1996/97 年 - 第一部分：切尔西震撼人心的夏天
news.body_en: It is 30 years since one of the most memorable and emotive seasons in the history of Chelsea Football Club. Our 1996/97 campaign was a tale of tragedy, transfers and, at its end, a long-sought-after major trophy. It is a story we will be retelling over the coming months through our archive of first-hand interviews. The words come from the very people who lived that momentous campaign: the players on the pitch, the coaches in the dugout, and the supporters in the stand. Our five long reads will focus on different subjects: the summer of ’96; the death of Matthew Harding; the arrival of Gianfranco Zola; the FA Cup comeback against Liverpool; and the 1997 FA Cup final, which provided a fitting finale. We start here in the weeks leading up to the new season, which followed hot on the heels of Euro ’96, held in England. It was a tournament that proved significant for this country on and off the pitch, and it was noteworthy for Chelsea, too. Newly appointed player-manager Ruud Gullit was a pundit for the BBC throughout the tournament, and at its conclusion, the Blues' outgoing boss, Glenn Hoddle, was to take charge of the Three Lions. Football was enjoying its finest hour in England for many decades, and we start by hearing from the DJ Trevor Nelson, a Chelsea fanatic, on what the mood was like during that balmy summer month. Nelson: I think the summer of '96 was one of the best summers in living memory, just because the football took over. It was the most patriotic I've ever been. I was actually imagining winning the thing! I think a lot of people started thinking, “We're going to win this”. I was thinking about Trafalgar Square, “Would I, wouldn't I,” you know, it was a bit like that. There was a genuine feeling that was the nearest we got to '66 in terms of the country. We'd heard all about it, but no one had ever witnessed it. There was cause for hope off the pitch, too, as Chelsea's club historian Rick Glanvill explains. Glanvill: It was a very inclusive tournament. It was all about getting young people in there, about appealing to women. It was a really interesting way that they pitched it, really. I think what they were trying to do was to make a break from the past. The image of English football in the eighties was from Heysel, for example, of hooliganism and run-down stadia. On the back of the Taylor report, where stadiums were being improved, and Euro '96, there was a real sense of renewal in English football. The legendary commentator Martin Tyler recalls the sense of anticipation ahead of the new Premier League season starting. Tyler: It wasn't that long since Blackburn Rovers had been champions. Manchester United were embarking in the early part of their domination of the Premier League in the nineties and the noughties, and the thought of Chelsea winning the league title was crazy. I was alive when they won it in 1955. Such a long time. People will have no recollection of it, really. “Oh, don't forget they won the league in 1955." Glanvill: There was a sense that football was returning to something like it probably had been in the 1930s to the 1950s and '60s, where it was part of the mainstream culture. At the forefront of this renovation, if you like, was Chelsea. Now, Chelsea was a side which finished 11th, 14th, 11th in seasons up to this point. There had been a revolution taking place under Glenn Hoddle since 1993. The whole explosion of money in the Premier League hadn't quite happened then - that's important to remember. But the foreign influence was coming, and in Chelsea's case, it arrived with Ruud Gullit. Nelson: I remember when Ruud Gullit signed for Chelsea. I remember coming to the Bridge, and Ruud Gullit did an Eddie Newton-style stepover. Ruud did it in his sleep. I looked at my mate and said, “We've got Ruud Gullit playing for us. It's amazing.” He was so lazily brilliant. He barely looked like he breathed in or out. He just did things. Gullit, arguably the most significant signing the club had ever made when he joined from Sampdoria in 1995, was clear in his motivations for moving to Stamford Bridge. Gullit: Glenn Hoddle, I think I admired him as a player and also what he was trying to do with Chelsea. I had some information about where Chelsea was and how London was, and it was also, for me, an important turn in my life. I wanted to have my life back. That meant that at the moment I was in Italy, everybody was on me, and it was hard to have an own life. And therefore, when I made that choice, I thought, “Okay, I go into something totally different.” I liked the English mentality, almost similar with the Dutch, so, "let's see what happens". The first year – I felt like a boy again. You must realise that when I played in Italy, in Milan, that was hard work. That was pressure every game, and it was like if you had a draw, then hell broke loose. Everybody was screaming and shouting and meetings and everything. We were under pressure all the time. And I remember one of the first games at Chelsea that I think we lost or we drew, and then the coach said, “Okay, bad luck. Next time, better.” And I was like, “Bad luck?” That was a relief. It was like there was no pressure, and therefore I could, I think, enjoy the game even more. The English game suited me also, but also the appreciation around it, and that everything what you'd done and what you wanted to do was good in the eyes of the fans and also of your own players. So it was like playing on a schoolyard. And I remember that Gavin Peacock came to me in a game. He said, "Look, Ruud, how is it possible? You are always unmarked. How do you do that?" I explained it was just the fact that I understood the game. It's also your experience of the game, that you know where it's crowded. You have to be somewhere else. You have to think two steps ahead, and therefore, if you go in that position, the ball will come automatically there. It was nice also to explain these things to the players. Gullit’s footballing acumen was one of the reasons why he emerged as a frontrunner to replace Glenn Hoddle when it was announced the graceful former midfielder would be taking charge of England once Euro '96 was over. Hoddle had arrived at Chelsea as player-manager in the summer of 1993, as football was entering an era of new possibilities following the birth of the Premier League and the expansion of European club competitions. He was a football philosopher and saw great potential in Chelsea, quickly implementing a root-and-branch revolution that radically reshaped many different aspects of the football club, as well as the mindset of the supporters. He would be a tough act to follow. When considering his replacement, it later emerged the board initially turned to Sampdoria's Sven-Goran Eriksson, with a view to Gullit working as a player-coach under him to help build on the foundations Hoddle had laid. Press speculation at the time put George Graham in the frame for the job, but the fans had other ideas. They wanted one man, and one man only. Glanvill: I always like to say he was the first publicly-elected manager because at the last match of the season, when it was clear Glenn Hoddle was going and the chairman had ideas about who he wanted to take over at the club, there'd been a rumour that Ruud Gullit, who was a player at the time, might want to be the player-manager. Gullit: It was strange because I didn't know what it is to be a manager or to be a coach. I didn't know. And I was like, “You want something that I don't know what it's all about.” It was just, you know, enjoying the game. And I felt pressure also, from the players and from the board. I was thinking about it. I was going home. I was going to a store. I said, “What do I have to do?” I'd never done it. So I thought about it, and I had no real quality time to think about it because there was this pressure on me. And then when people persuaded me to do it, I said, “Okay, I will do it. I will do it. I'll do whatever comes into me to do.” Tyler: There was an opportunity for Chelsea to step a bit more into the limelight. Glenn obviously was a high-profile manager, but they were a mid-table team, and Ruud Gullit had been associated with success all his life, so he wasn't coming to be in charge of a mid-table team. That was the impression at the time. Gullit the player wasn't about to retire, and so, to ensure he could continue to play at the highest level and focus on the overall direction of the team on the pitch, certain responsibilities that come with being a manager were delegated to others. Ade Mafe, a 200-meter Olympic finalist in 1984 at the age of just 17, was recruited from a Kings Road health club to look after the player's fitness programme. Elsewhere, Colin Hutchinson, the much-respected managing director, took a more hands-on approach to the recruitment of players. Hutchinson: It was a very small team, we didn't have millions of scouts. We probably had half a dozen. A lot of it was information gathering, having very good contacts with agents and clubs and things around Europe, and having the philosophy that decisions could be made quickly. It was really down to me to go to [chairman] Ken Bates, and if he said, “Okay,” then we got on and did it. Some clubs would have committees where they were discussing deals for days, where we would say, "Yeah, we're going to do it," and go and do it. Gullit: I knew what I needed to strengthen the team, especially in the spine, and that's what I did. And I tried to get all these players. Glanvill: So Ruud Gullit came in on a wave of goodwill, and the extension of everything that had happened since 1995, really, when Gullit had come in, Mark Hughes had come in, and we'd started to refresh the squad, bring in real world-class players, continued. Gianluca Vialli signed two days after he'd lifted the European Cup as the captain of Juventus. Hutchinson: It was an interesting one. Ruud wasn't sure, but in the end, he decided to give it a whirl. I remember I was on holiday in Cyprus because it was close season. He was with Juventus, and they were playing in the Champions League final in Rome. So I left my family in Cyprus, boarded a flight, went to Rome. He got me tickets for the match, went to the match. They won 1-0. Then the next day, went from Rome to Turin and signed him. The next addition to the squad was Frank Leboeuf, a muscular, tall French defender who read the game superbly and was confident in possession. He cost Chelsea £2.5 million. Hutchinson: I went out to Strasbourg to do the deal, and then I went to a hotel, I think it was in Wigan or somewhere, to actually sign him. Leboeuf: In fact, it was a very easy decision. I was in England for Euro '96, and I had some teams in Italy interested in me, like Lazio, and I had Betis interested in me. When Ruud Gullit contacted me, I was in my room, and I said, “Okay.” I didn't even talk about the money and the contract. I said, “Okay, I want to come.” I never put one foot in London, but I was ready to come because, I don't know, it was something obvious. I had this energy, this feeling, you know, that it would be great. And I wanted to learn English. My kids also, I wanted them to speak English. It was, for me, a big challenge and a beautiful opportunity to do something with that club. And so I signed without visiting the facilities, without knowing anything but the names of the players and the fact that they wanted me. Glanvill: One of the most interesting signings was Roberto Di Matteo, because he was an Italy international and he'd been wrenched away from Lazio. Lazio supporters protested and tried to block his car leaving. This was a man in his prime, and for Chelsea supporters, that was quite a significant moment. It wasn't someone who was in his 30s, who was coming for a payday. This was someone who thought, "Do you know what? I see prospects here. I see the chance of winning silverware." Di Matteo: For me, it was just important that the club wanted me, that the manager wanted me, and I saw that there was an opportunity to be successful. That was very important for me as a professional, to win trophies, to win something. It was quite an easy decision for me. It was very important that Ruud Gullit was the manager. Very important that the club moved very, very fast to sign me. And I didn't really know much about London or England. That was all new to me, but that was secondary. Important was the professional aspect of it. The chairman was very ambitious. The club was ambitious. The manager. So that was good enough for me. Hutchinson: That was a very complicated transfer because it wasn’t the norm in those days for current Italian internationals to leave the country, and it went on for quite a long time. I remember, to finalise the deal, I went to Rome, to the president’s apartment in the centre of Rome, and it took us about five hours to thrash out a deal. And even then, Roberto wanted to think more about it. He and I and his entourage, we came out of the building, and we got spat upon because everything is in the public domain in Italy. But eventually, he signed, and a very good signing. Of the existing squad, no player had made more appearances for Chelsea than club stalwart Steve Clarke, who had arrived in 1987. He immediately felt the new additions’ impact. Clarke: As a player, you always want to see good players coming in to give you competition. They were three good players, three big names, and to have those people come into the club was exciting. Tyler: There's always a tinge of glamour around the place, but it was usually in the crowd rather than on the pitch. There were always film stars, West End actors, TV stars. Raquel Welch on one famous occasion! It always had that feel about it, but this was a real chance to glamorise it on the pitch. It didn't happen straight away, but it clearly was a statement of intent. Glanvill: The transition that was taking place at Chelsea was this: older players who had the quality and adaptability to work under Ruud Gullit's new methodology, such as Dennis Wise, Steve Clarke, were still there. A lot of the old guard, if you like, younger players, some of them had been around a bit too long. Some players who were maybe not quite of the standard that was required were let go. Some of the younger players who had proved that they could live with the best quality football, such as Eddie Newton, Frank Sinclair, they retained their places. It really was a revamp, a massive revamp from the team that had lost the FA Cup in 93/94. The Premier League may be awash with players from all corners of the globe now, but in the mid-1990s, things were very different, with the three-foreigner rule stipulating that clubs could only name three players from outside the UK and Ireland in their matchday squad. That all changed in December 1995, though, and Chelsea were one of the first teams to take full advantage. As a result, the existing players needed to raise their levels. Kevin Hitchcock, a long-serving goalkeeper whose Chelsea career was hampered by injury, quickly noticed a difference. Hitchcock: Things changed. Diets changed. The way we trained was different. They’d be in the gym, stretching, warming up, and then everybody did it. Homegrown, Hammersmith-born Eddie Newton had established himself in Chelsea’s midfield earlier in the ‘90s. Newton: There was slowly a different ilk of player that was coming into the club, with more experience, played at a higher level, and therefore, everything within the club started to go and function towards a higher level. Chelsea were no longer just a team that could win on their day. Chelsea were now becoming a force to be taken seriously. When we were growing up at the club, we were so used to not just English players, we had a lot of Irish, Scottish players. When we were growing up, they were foreign! For me, seeing foreign players was not a big thing. The biggest thing for me was watching when Ruud Gullit came through the door, because he was my idol. When he came through the door, my jaw dropped. Vialli is iconic, Dan Petrescu, Ruud Gullit, Mark Hughes, this ilk of player was coming through the door, and now we knew that the club had a different kind of focus. The players within the group that were British kind of accepted it quite well. I didn't really feel there was any cliques. Ruudy was very big on that straight away to make sure that didn't happen. Among those playing a crucial part in helping the new signings settle were senior pros Clarke and captain Dennis Wise. Wise: I think at first a lot of the Italians couldn't believe how relaxed it was. It was a lot more intense in Italy than it was over here. You got a little bit more leeway, and they enjoyed themselves, and it was important for them to enjoy it. Clarke: We just helped them to understand the culture of the club, what the club was about, what we were trying to do, how you behaved in England. I think lots of just little details that probably and obviously made an impact on those players. Di Matteo: We tried very hard from the beginning. We tried to learn the language. Because I speak German, it was a bit easier for me because many words are similar. But we tried very hard to learn the language. That was important so that we could just blend into the team and make it easy for everybody. Vialli: When you try to learn a new language and you're like 12, 14, you're like a sponge, so you absorb and you learn much quicker. When you're 30, 32, then you're a little bit lazier, and you don't get things so quickly like when you're a child. I didn't find it easy at all. London is a very special place where you can certainly survive even though you don't speak a word of English because if you're Italian, there are enough Italians out there to keep you busy and help you out in case you need anything. There were so many foreigners at the club that I could speak Spanish and Italian and really have enough conversations even without knowing the language, but then I think I put a lot of effort in it because I wanted to be able to communicate because there's so much I can tell. Wise: I remember I used to take Luca to the pictures every Friday and go for a pizza. It was just making sure that people were comfortable. They come to a different environment, they've come over from overseas, and they need to relax, and they need to enjoy themselves. Di Matteo: The English boys, the British boys, they tried to make it easier for us, and they helped us out a lot, and we were like a big family. That helped on the pitch as well to get some results. Leboeuf: I came to play to have an English feeling. Even if we had a European kind of football way, we were led by Dennis Wise. We were following Dennis and Steve Clarke and Mark Hughes because we wanted to learn English. We wanted to appreciate the time in England and not being a team who plays like an Italian side in England. Newton: Real success was behind the scenes that we were able to amalgamate and not get drawn up into little groups. Then you could see what happened on the pitch. It started to come together quicker than most clubs. I think a lot of clubs initially, in the beginning, struggled when they started bringing foreigners over. I do believe it would have been that the British trying to hold fort and foreigners feeling that they're not accepted. So I think that would have been happening behind closed doors where it wasn't so much like that at our place. While the players were settling off the pitch, Gullit himself had to adapt to a new role completely alien to him. In his column in the club's official newspaper of the time, Onside, he pinpointed two necessary attributes above all others. ‘To wear the colours of Chelsea must be an honour,’ Gullit wrote, adding that, ‘Everyone must be aware of the dedication needed to become a better player.’ Defender Frank Sinclair remembers what the new player-manager had to go through. Sinclair: It was a difficult transformation for him because all of a sudden you go from being one of the boys to having to call the shots, upsetting players because you can't keep everybody happy being only able to select 11 players. I felt he dealt with it quite well. Obviously, his experience in the game was unbelievable. World Player of the Year. He'd won the Champions League. He'd won the Euros and stuff like that. So his credentials were unbelievable. He came in with his own ideas, and rightfully, he tagged it sexy football. We bought into it with a smile on our faces, but we understood what he wanted to do. He wanted to make the way we played a lot more attractive, and with the background he had, we trusted in his ideas. It was excellent. He still played often enough that he had an input on the pitch as well, but realistically, you could see the transformation of him turning into a coach and wanting to get the side playing the way that he wanted us to play. Gullit: When I was at the European Championships for a game, Czech Republic against Portugal, I said that Portugal play sexy football. And that term, that phrase followed me all these years after that. Glanvill: You looked at Ruud Gullit, over six-foot tall, great dreadlocks, he looked the absolute business. You couldn't help but listen to him and feel inspired, and you could see that the players felt the same way about that. Gullit's effervescence had been a trademark of his playing days, and it was a characteristic he wanted to maintain now he had the top gig. Gullit: If you win and you play well and you do things together, it's the biggest joy you have. You can't do it on your own. You need your players around you. You need everybody around you. Not only the 11 players, but all the 20 players, 22, whatever. You need them all. So I need you to have also fun with each other, good banter with each other, but be serious in the moment that it is. Look, we are all little kids. And of course it's work, but you work so much better if you also enjoy what you're doing. And it is, come on. Who doesn't want to have your job outside playing football? Come on. What is not to enjoy about it? There were some detractors who questioned Gullit’s personality and management style, however. Gullit: That's how I am. I laughed about people that always thought I was arrogant. I was thinking, “What do you mean? You don't know me. I'm very relaxed. I'm very open.” Maybe it's sometimes because I try to protect myself that I don't want to show myself that much, but I'm very, very relaxed. And the thing is, players need to know that it's about something. It's not here only to be relaxed and nice and laughing and everything. No. The most important thing is that you work when you work. As a coach, I tried to transmit that fact to the team. And they felt relaxed. That's why I think they also got all these wins. It was slowly, slowly trying to build up something. And I know they were doing their best all the time. Dan Petrescu, one of many players from that time who subsequently went into management themselves, benefited from Gullit's philosophy. A forward-thinking, right-sided player and Chelsea's first from overseas to reach 200 appearances for the club, the Romanian was given plenty of reign to join the attack. Petrescu: It was a pleasure to go to training. I enjoyed everything. It is not a mistake they said we play sexy football because he liked to play football. He didn't like to defend. He just liked to play all the time. This is maybe also Dutch mentality of the coaches, to play nice football, and he brings something from these coaches and from his mentality. Just to enjoy it, go out, enjoy, and play football. Elsewhere, Leboeuf was not only tasked with shoring up the centre of defence. He had been voted European Libero of the Year by Italian newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport in 1995. His assurance in possession and eye for a defence-splitting long pass would prove crucial for the way Gullit wanted his team to play, even if the risks Leboeuf took sometimes left Chelsea hearts in mouths. Leboeuf: I didn't have an education as a defender. I was a midfield player, and even played up front. So I was pretty offensive. The start of the offensive attack is very important. You give the rhythm, and I really wanted to do something special. People didn’t like it, but I think it changed a little bit the game of Chelsea. Further upfield, Gullit got to work on maximising the captain’s potential. Gullit: Wisey played very good football. I had a big argument with him. He was playing in a way I didn't like. He was still playing the Wimbledon way, the Crazy Gang way. A couple of times I said to him I wanted him to play in a different way, and he didn’t do it. He didn't speak with me for about three weeks. He didn't want to speak with me at all. Then we have a common friend who we played golf with. He said to Wisey: “Go to his house, call him, because he hasn't got anything against you." He thought I had something against him. He thought I wanted to put only foreigners in there and not him, but I didn’t. So he called me, and came to my house. We had a drink, and I explained it to him. “Look, that Crazy Gang thing is over. You are one of the best players. You have to play with responsibility. You are captain. As a captain, you are an example for the rest. And I want you to play in a certain way that suits you very well: holding player, always keeping the ball, trying to make a link to the front man. And if you play well, I assure you will play also in the national team.” Hoddle's influence earlier in the '90s is widely credited with kickstarting the modern Chelsea we know today, but Gullit did make some fundamental changes, none more so, arguably, than modifying the players' day-to-day routine. They were to all eat together at the club's Harlington training ground between sessions, encouraged to talk football, and in turn develop a sense of autonomy about their game. Gullit didn't want to adopt a paternalistic approach, rather one centred on trust and self-management. It was one of the reasons he got rid of the club dietitian when he took over. Gullit: I just wanted them to think about their own game but also about the team. I want to know what they're thinking. I don't want any robots. A robot doesn't help me. On the pitch, things change, so when it changes, I need players who take responsibility on the pitch. Gullit's methodology paid off, particularly at Stamford Bridge, where the team lost only twice all season, and an away win at Old Trafford in the November proved the Blues could mix it with the best on their day. Alex Ferguson said of all the teams Manchester United faced that season, Chelsea had the ‘best imagination in the final third.’ Gullit: I have seen games that were unbelievable. Of course, Liverpool [in the FA Cup] was the best example of that, but I enjoyed watching them. That's why I withdrew myself more, to see what I needed to improve and what I needed to do. Clarke: It was great to play in, and we played some great football, pass and move. Played with freedom. Played without fear. It was the start of a really good period for the club and for the team. I still speak to a lot of supporters now who speak about that time, the end of Glenn's reign and the start of Ruud Gullit's reign as some of the best football that Chelsea have played in recent memory. To be associated with that team and remembered in that way is great. Nelson: I think for Chelsea fans, I can speak for myself, it felt like we finally came to the party. I think if you're really honest about where we were, we were the third club in London. We were always fighting for third spot in London. Arsenal were out on their own, no doubt about it. Tottenham, just because they'd done the Double in when was it, ‘61? And they won a couple of cups, so they'd still won more than us. We were third, really. That hurt. The mood now was that we had something special here. We haven't got just one sporadic good striker like Kerry Dixon, or we haven't got just a Ray Wilkins in midfield, or a sporadic great goal. No. We've got a team. And it was exciting. It wasn't just that we had a team. It's the brand of football. We were playing the sort of football that neutrals would want to come and watch, which is quite a compliment for Chelsea. It was a love affair, the start of a real love affair with this whole new international team, because I think it was the mid-'90s where we really became an international club. I love that team. They put the swagger back into Chelsea. The Kings Road, the Fulham Road, the last time we had that sort of swag was the early '70s with [Alan] Hudson, with Ossy [Peter Osgood] and Charlie Cooke and [Ian] Hutchinson. There was a 20-year gap, and then we got our swagger back. In the second long read retelling the story of the 1996/97 season, we will remember Matthew Harding on the 30th anniversary of his tragic death…
news.body_zh: 切尔西足球俱乐部历史上最难忘、最感人的赛季之一已经过去 30 年了。我们的 1996/97 赛季是一个充满悲剧、转会的故事，最终赢得了人们渴望已久的重要奖杯。我们将在未来几个月通过第一手采访档案重述这个故事。这句话出自那些经历过那场重要战役的人之口：球场上的球员、教练席上的教练和看台上的支持者。我们的五篇长篇读物将关注不同的主题：96 年的夏天；马修·哈丁去世；詹弗兰科·佐拉的到来；足总杯对阵利物浦的复出； 1997 年的足总杯决赛也为球队画上了圆满的句号。我们从新赛季开始前的几周开始，新赛季紧随在英格兰举行的 96 年欧洲杯之后。事实证明，这是一场对这个国家无论场内场外都意义重大的赛事，对于切尔西来说也是值得注意的。新任命的球员兼主教练路德·古利特在整个赛事期间一直是 BBC 的评论员，比赛结束后，蓝军即将卸任的主帅格伦·霍德尔将执掌三狮军团。英格兰足球正享受着几十年来最美好的时光，我们首先听听切尔西狂热分子 DJ 特雷弗·尼尔森 (Trevor Nelson) 讲述那个温暖的夏季的气氛。尼尔森：我认为 96 年的夏天是人们记忆中最美好的夏天之一，因为足球占据了主导地位。这是我有史以来最爱国的一次。我实际上正在想象赢得胜利！我想很多人开始想，“我们会赢的”。我在想特拉法加广场，“我会，我不会，”你知道，有点像那样。有一种真实的感觉，就这个国家而言，这是我们最接近 66 年的感觉。我们听说过这一切，但没有人亲眼目睹过。正如切尔西俱乐部历史学家里克·格兰维尔所解释的那样，球场外也充满希望。格兰维尔：这是一场包容性很强的比赛。这一切都是为了让年轻人进入那里，为了吸引女性。他们的推销方式真的很有趣。我认为他们试图做的是与过去决裂。例如，八十年代英国足球的形象来自于海瑟尔，流氓行为和破旧的体育场。在泰勒报告的背景下，球场得到了改善，而96年欧洲杯也让英格兰足球有了真正的复兴感。传奇评论员马丁·泰勒回忆起新赛季英超联赛开始前的期待感。泰勒：布莱克本流浪者队获得冠军并没有多久。曼联在上世纪九十年代开始统治英超联赛的早期，切尔西赢得联赛冠军的想法是疯狂的。 1955 年他们赢得冠军时我还活着。已经很久了。人们真的不会记得它。 “哦，别忘了他们在 1955 年赢得了联赛冠军。”格兰维尔：有一种感觉，足球正在回到 20 世纪 30 年代到 1950 年代和 60 年代的状态，当时足球是主流文化的一部分。如果你愿意的话，处于这次改造的最前沿的是切尔西。到目前为止，切尔西是一支在赛季中排名第 11、第 14、第 11 的球队。自 1993 年以来，格伦·霍德尔 (Glenn Hoddle) 的领导下发生了一场革命。当时英超联赛的资金爆炸还没有完全发生 - 记住这一点很重要。但外国的影响力正在到来，就切尔西而言，它是随着路德·古利特而来的。尼尔森：我记得古力特加盟切尔西的时候。我记得来到大桥时，路德·古利特做了埃迪·牛顿式的跨步动作。路德是在睡梦中做到的。我看着我的队友说：“我们有路德·古力特为我们效力。这太棒了。”他是如此懒惰的聪明人。他看起来几乎没有呼吸。他只是做了事。古力特 1995 年从桑普多利亚加盟，可以说是俱乐部历史上最重要的签约，他转会斯坦福桥的动机很明确。古力特：格伦·霍德尔，我想我很钦佩他作为一名球员以及他在切尔西所做的事情。我了解了一些关于切尔西在哪里以及伦敦怎么样的信息，对我来说，这也是我人生中的一个重要转折。我想恢复我的生活。这意味着我现在在意大利，每个人都在关注我，很难拥有自己的生活。 因此，当我做出这个选择时，我想：“好吧，我会做一些完全不同的事情。”我喜欢英国人的心态，几乎与荷兰人相似，所以，“让我们看看会发生什么”。第一年——我又感觉自己像个男孩了。你必须意识到，当我在意大利、米兰踢球时，那是艰苦的工作。每场比赛都是压力，就好像如果你打平了，那么地狱就会爆发。每个人都在尖叫、喊叫、开会等等。我们一直承受着压力。我记得在切尔西的第一场比赛，我认为我们输了或者平了，然后教练说，“好吧，运气不好。下次，更好。”我当时想，“运气不好？”这真是一种解脱。就好像没有压力一样，因此我认为我可以更加享受比赛。英格兰比赛也适合我，而且也适合我，而且你所做的一切和你想做的一切在球迷和你自己的球员眼中都是好的。所以这就像在校园里玩耍一样。我记得加文·皮科克在一场比赛中来找我。他说：“你看，路德，这怎么可能？你总是没有被标记。你是怎么做到的？”我解释说这只是我理解这个游戏的事实。这也是你的游戏体验，你知道哪里拥挤。你必须在别的地方。你必须提前考虑两步，因此，如果你走到那个位置，球就会自动到达那里。向玩家解释这些事情也很高兴。当宣布这位优雅的前中场球员将在 96 年欧洲杯结束后执掌英格兰队时，古利特的足球天赋是他成为取代格伦·霍德尔的领跑者的原因之一。 1993 年夏天，霍德尔以球员兼教练的身份来到切尔西，当时随着英超联赛的诞生和欧洲俱乐部赛事的扩展，足球界正在进入一个充满新可能性的时代。他是一位足球哲学家，看到了切尔西的巨大潜力，迅速实施了一场彻底的革命，从根本上重塑了足球俱乐部的许多不同方面以及球迷的心态。他的行为很难追随。在考虑他的替代者时，后来发现董事会最初转向了桑普多利亚的斯文-戈兰·埃里克森，希望古力特在他手下担任球员兼教练，以帮助巩固霍德尔奠定的基础。当时的媒体猜测乔治·格雷厄姆可能会担任这一职务，但球迷们却有其他想法。他们想要一个人，而且只需要一个人。格兰维尔：我总是喜欢说他是第一位公开选举的主教练，因为在本赛季的最后一场比赛中，当格伦·霍德尔明确要离开并且主席对他想接替俱乐部的人有想法时，有传言称当时还是球员的路德·古利特可能想成为球员兼主教练。古利特：这很奇怪，因为我不知道成为一名主教练或教练意味着什么。我不知道。我当时想，“你想要一些我不知道它到底是什么的东西。”你知道，这只是享受比赛。我也感受到了来自球员和董事会的压力。我正在想。我正要回家。我正要去一家商店。我说：“我该怎么办？”我从来没有这样做过。所以我思考了这个问题，但我没有真正的时间去思考它，因为我承受着这种压力。然后，当人们说服我这样做时，我说：“好吧，我会做的。我会做的。我会做任何我想做的事。”泰勒：切尔西有机会进一步成为众人瞩目的焦点。格伦显然是一位备受瞩目的主教练，但他们是一支中游球队，而古力特一生都与成功联系在一起，所以他不会来执掌一支中游球队。当时的印象就是这样。古力特这位球员并不打算退役，因此，为了确保他能够继续发挥最高水平并专注于球队在球场上的整体方向，作为教练所承担的某些职责被委托给了其他人。 1984 年，年仅 17 岁的阿德·马菲 (Ade Mafe) 就进入了 200 米奥运会决赛，他是从国王路 (Kings Road) 的一家健身俱乐部招募来负责球员的健身计划的。在其他方面，备受尊敬的董事总经理科林·哈钦森(Colin Hutchinson)在招募球员方面采取了更加亲力亲为的方法。哈钦森：那是一支非常小的球队，我们没有数百万球探。我们可能有六个。 其中很大一部分是信息收集，与欧洲各地的经纪人、俱乐部和事物保持良好的联系，并拥有可以快速做出决定的理念。我真的决定去找[主席]肯·贝茨，如果他说“好吧”，那么我们就继续做下去。有些俱乐部会设立委员会，他们会花几天时间讨论交易，我们会说，“是的，我们会这么做”，然后就去做。古利特：我知道我需要什么来加强球队，特别是在脊柱方面，这就是我所做的。我试图吸引所有这些球员。格兰维尔：所以路德·古利特带着一波善意的到来，自1995年以来发生的一切的延续，真的，当古利特进来时，马克·休斯也进来了，我们开始更新阵容，引进真正的世界级球员，继续。詹卢卡·维亚利 (Gianluca Vialli) 在作为尤文图斯队长举起欧洲冠军杯两天后签约。哈钦森：这是一件有趣的事。路德不确定，但最终他决定尝试一下。我记得我在塞浦路斯度假，因为当时是淡季。他当时效力于尤文图斯队，当时他们正在罗马参加欧冠决赛。于是我离开了塞浦路斯的家人，登上了飞往罗马的航班。他给我买了比赛门票，然后就去看了比赛。他们以 1-0 获胜。然后第二天，从罗马前往都灵签下了他。球队的下一个成员是弗兰克·勒伯夫（Frank Leboeuf），他是一位肌肉发达、身材高大的法国后卫，他对比赛的阅读能力很强，并且对控球充满信心。他让切尔西损失了250万英镑。哈钦森：我去了斯特拉斯堡做这笔交易，然后我去了一家酒店，我认为是在维冈或其他地方，真正签下了他。 Leboeuf：事实上，这是一个非常简单的决定。我在英格兰参加96年欧洲杯，意大利有一些球队对我​​感兴趣，比如拉齐奥，贝蒂斯也对我感兴趣。当路德·古利特联系我时，我正在房间里，我说：“好吧。”我什至没有谈论金钱和合同。我说：“好吧，我想来。”我从未踏足过伦敦，但我已经准备好来了，因为，我不知道，这是显而易见的事情。我有这种能量，这种感觉，你知道，那会很棒。我想学英语。我的孩子们也是如此，我希望他们说英语。对我来说，这是一个巨大的挑战，也是一个与俱乐部一起做事的绝佳机会。所以我在没有参观设施的情况下就签约了，除了球员的名字和他们想要我的事实之外什么都不知道。格兰维尔：最有趣的签约之一是罗伯托·迪马特奥，因为他是一名意大利国脚，而且是从拉齐奥挖走的。拉齐奥的支持者抗议并试图阻止他的汽车离开。这是一个正值巅峰的人，对于切尔西的支持者来说，这是一个非常重要的时刻。这不是一个三十多岁的人，不是来发薪水的。这个人的想法是：“你知道吗？我在这里看到了前景。我看到了赢得奖杯的机会。”迪马特奥：对我来说，重要的是俱乐部想要我，主教练想要我，而且我看到了成功的机会。作为一名职业球员，这对我来说非常重要，赢得奖杯，赢得一些东西。这对我来说是一个很容易的决定。古力特担任主教练非常重要。非常重要的是，俱乐部非常非常快地签下了我。我对伦敦或英国也不太了解。这对我来说是全新的，但那是次要的。重要的是它的专业方面。主席非常有野心。俱乐部雄心勃勃。经理。所以这对我来说已经足够好了。哈钦森：那是一次非常复杂的转会，因为当时意大利国脚离开意大利并不常见，而且这种情况持续了很长一段时间。我记得，为了敲定协议，我去了罗马，去了位于罗马市中心的总统公寓，我们花了大约五个小时才敲定了协议。即便如此，罗伯托还是想更多地考虑一下。他和我以及他的随行人员，我们走出大楼，我们被吐口水，因为在意大利，一切都属于公共领域。但最终他还是签约了，而且是一笔非常好的签约。在现有阵容中，没有哪位球员比 1987 年加盟的俱乐部中坚史蒂夫·克拉克 (Steve Clarke) 代表切尔西出场次数更多。他立即感受到了新援的影响。克拉克：作为一名球员，你总是希望看到优秀的球员进来给你带来竞争。 他们是三位优秀的球员，三位大牌球员，让这些人加入俱乐部真是令人兴奋。泰勒：这个地方总是充满着一丝魅力，但通常是在人群中而不是在球场上。总是有电影明星、西区演员、电视明星。拉蔻儿·韦尔奇 (Raquel Welch) 在一个著名的场合！它总是有这种感觉，但这是一个在球场上展现它魅力的真正机会。这不是立即发生的，但它显然是一个意图声明。格兰维尔：切尔西正在发生的转变是这样的：那些有能力和适应能力在路德·古利特的新方法下工作的老球员，比如丹尼斯·怀斯、史蒂夫·克拉克，仍然留在那里。很多老后卫，如果你喜欢的话，还有年轻球员，他们中的一些人已经存在了太久了。一些可能达不到要求标准的球员被解雇了。一些年轻球员已经证明了他们可以忍受最优质的足球，比如埃迪·牛顿、弗兰克·辛克莱，他们保住了自己的位置。这确实是一次改造，对93/94年失去足总杯的球队来说是一次巨大的改造。现在的英超联赛可能充斥着来自世界各地的球员，但在 90 年代中期，情况大不相同，三名外国人规则规定，俱乐部在比赛阵容中只能提名三名来自英国和爱尔兰以外的球员。然而，这一切在 1995 年 12 月发生了变化，切尔西是第一批充分利用这一优势的球队之一。因此，现有的玩家需要提升自己的等级。凯文·希区柯克 (Kevin Hitchcock) 是一位长期效力切尔西的门将，他的切尔西职业生涯因伤病而受到阻碍，他很快就注意到了其中的差异。希区柯克：事情发生了变化。饮食习惯改变了。我们训练的方式不一样。他们会在健身房里伸展身体、热身，然后每个人都这样做。出生于哈默史密斯的埃迪·牛顿 (Eddie Newton) 早在上世纪 90 年代就已经在切尔西的中场站稳了脚跟。牛顿：慢慢地，有不同类型的球员进入俱乐部，他们有更多的经验，在更高的水平上踢球，因此，俱乐部内的一切都开始朝着更高的水平发展。切尔西不再只是一支能够在当天获胜的球队。切尔西现在正成为一支值得认真对待的力量。当我们在俱乐部长大时，我们不仅习惯了英格兰球员，还有很多爱尔兰、苏格兰球员。当我们长大的时候，他们是外国人！对我来说，见到外国球员并不是什么大事。对我来说最重要的事情就是看着古利特走进门，因为他是我的偶像。当他进门时，我的下巴都惊掉了。维亚利是标志性的球员，丹·佩特雷斯库、路德·古力特、马克·休斯，这些球员都在门外，现在我们知道俱乐部有不同的关注点。小组中的英国选手也很好地接受了这一点。我真的不觉得有任何派系。鲁迪立即对此非常重视，以确保这种情况不会发生。在帮助新援安顿下来的过程中发挥着关键作用的人包括资深职业球员克拉克和队长丹尼斯·怀斯。怀斯：我想一开始很多意大利人都不敢相信这是多么轻松。意大利的情况比这里激烈得多。你有更多的余地，他们会很享受，享受这对他们来说很重要。克拉克：我们只是帮助他们了解俱乐部的文化，俱乐部的宗旨是什么，我们想要做什么，以及你在英格兰的表现如何。我认为很多小细节可能而且明显地对这些球员产生了影响。迪马特奥：我们从一开始就非常努力。我们尝试学习这门语言。因为我说德语，所以对我来说更容易一些，因为很多单词都是相似的。但我们非常努力地学习这门语言。这很重要，这样我们就可以融入团队并让每个人都感到轻松。维亚利：当你尝试学习一门新语言时，你就像 12 岁、14 岁一样，你就像一块海绵，所以你吸收并且学得更快。当你30岁、32岁的时候，你会有点懒，你不会像小时候那样很快就能得到东西。我发现这根本不容易。伦敦是一个非常特别的地方，即使你不会说一句英语，你也肯定可以生存下来，因为如果你是意大利人，那里有足够多的意大利人让你忙碌起来，并在你需要任何东西时帮助你。 俱乐部里有很多外国人，我可以说西班牙语和意大利语，即使不懂语言，也能进行足够的对话，但后来我想我在这方面付出了很多努力，因为我希望能够沟通，因为我能说的东西太多了。 Wise：我记得我以前每周五都会带 Luca 去看电影，然后去吃披萨。这只是确保人们感到舒适。他们来到了不同的环境，他们从海外过来，他们需要放松，他们需要享受。迪马特奥：英国男孩，英国男孩，他们试图让我们变得更容易，他们帮助了我们很多，我们就像一个大家庭。这也有助于在球场上取得一些成果。 Leboeuf：我来踢球是为了有一种英国的感觉。即使我们有欧洲式的足球方式，我们也是由丹尼斯·怀斯领导的。我们关注丹尼斯、史蒂夫·克拉克和马克·休斯是因为我们想学习英语。我们想要享受在英格兰度过的时光，而不是成为一支像意大利球队一样在英格兰踢球的球队。牛顿：真正的成功是在幕后，我们能够团结起来，而不是分成小团体。然后你就可以看到球场上发生了什么。它开始比大多数俱乐部更快地聚集在一起。我认为很多俱乐部一开始在引进外国人时都遇到了困难。我确实相信，英国人会试图坚守阵地，而外国人则感觉自己不被接受。所以我认为这会是在闭门的情况下发生的，而在我们这里情况并非如此。当球员们在场外安顿下来时，古利特本人却不得不适应一个与他完全陌生的新角色。在当时俱乐部官方报纸《Onside》的专栏中，他指出了两个最重要的特征。 “能够穿上切尔西队的球衣一定是一种荣幸，”古力特写道，并补充道，“每个人都必须意识到成为一名更好的球员所需的奉献精神。”后卫弗兰克·辛克莱尔记得这位新球员兼主教练必须经历的事情。辛克莱：这对他来说是一个艰难的转变，因为突然间你从男孩中的一员变成了必须发号施令的人，这让球员们感到不安，因为你不能让每个人都高兴，只能选择 11 名球员。我感觉他处理得很好。显然，他在比赛中的经历令人难以置信。年度世界足球先生。他赢得了冠军联赛。他赢得了欧洲杯之类的东西。所以他的资历令人难以置信。他带着自己的想法进来，理所当然地，他给足球贴上了性感的标签。我们面带微笑地接受了它，但我们明白他想做什么。他想让我们的比赛方式更具吸引力，并且凭借他的背景，我们相信他的想法。太棒了。他仍然经常参加比赛，因此他在球场上也有贡献，但实际上，你可以看到他转变为一名教练，并希望让球队按照他希望我们踢的方式踢球。古力特：当我在欧洲杯捷克对阵葡萄牙的一场比赛中，我说葡萄牙踢的是性感足球。在那之后的这些年里，这个词、那个短语一直伴随着我。格兰维尔：你看看路德·古利特，身高超过六英尺，留着大辫子，他看起来绝对是生意人。你会情不自禁地听他讲话并受到启发，你可以看到球员们对此也有同样的感受。古力特的热情是他职业生涯的标志，现在他已经成为了顶级球员，他想保持这一特点。古利特：如果你赢了，打得很好，并且一起做事，那就是你最大的快乐。你不能自己做。你需要你的球员在你身边。你需要你身边的每一个人。不仅是 11 名球员，还有所有 20 名球员，22 名球员，等等。你需要它们。所以我需要你们彼此玩得开心，互相开玩笑，但在这一刻要严肃。瞧，我们都是小孩子。当然，这是工作，但如果你也喜欢你正在做的事情，你会工作得更好。确实如此，来吧。谁不想在踢足球之外拥有自己的工作呢？快点。有什么不值得享受的呢？然而，也有一些批评者质疑古力特的个性和管理风格。古利特：我就是这样的。我嘲笑那些总是认为我傲慢的人。我在想：“你什么意思？ 你不认识我。我很放松。我很开放。”也许有时候因为我想保护自己，所以不想表现得太多，但是我非常非常放松。问题是，玩家需要知道这是关于某事的。来这里不仅仅是为了放松、美好、欢笑等等。不，最重要的是当你工作的时候你就在工作。作为一名教练，我试图将这一事实传达给球队。他们感到轻松。这就是为什么我认为他们也获得了所有这些胜利。它正在慢慢地、慢慢地尝试建立一些东西。我知道他们一直在尽力而为。丹·佩特雷斯库（Dan Petrescu）是当时众多后来进入管理层的球员之一，他从古利特的哲学中受益匪浅。这位罗马尼亚人是一位具有前瞻性思维的右路球员，也是切尔西队中第一位为俱乐部出场次数达到 200 场的海外球员，他在进攻中拥有足够的统治力。佩特雷斯库：很高兴参加训练。我很享受一切。他们说我们踢性感足球并不是错误的，因为他喜欢踢足球。他不喜欢防守。他只是喜欢一直玩而已。这也许也是荷兰教练的心态，踢出漂亮的足球，他从这些教练和他的心态中带来了一些东西。只是为了享受它，出去，享受，踢足球。在其他地方，勒伯夫的任务不仅是支撑后防线。 1995年，他被意大利报纸《米兰体育报》评选为欧洲年度最佳自由人。他对控球的保证和对突破防线的长传的敏锐洞察力对于古力特希望他的球队的比赛方式至关重要，即使勒伯夫所冒的风险有时会让切尔西心惊肉跳。勒伯夫：我没有接受过后卫教育。我是一名中场球员，甚至踢前锋。所以我非常反感。进攻的开始非常重要。你给了节奏，我真的想做一些特别的事情。人们不喜欢它，但我认为它改变了切尔西的比赛。在前场，古利特开始致力于最大限度地发挥队长的潜力。古利特：威西踢得非常好。我和他大吵了一架。他以一种我不喜欢的方式打球。他仍然以温布尔登的方式、疯狂帮的方式打球。有几次我对他说我希望他以不同的方式打球，但他没有这么做。他大约三个星期没有和我说话。他根本不想和我说话。然后我们有一个共同的朋友，我们一起打高尔夫球。他对威西说：“去他家，给他打电话，因为他对你没有任何不满。”他以为我对他有什么敌意。他以为我只想让外国人在那里而不是他，但我没有。于是他打电话给我，来到我家。我们喝了一杯，我向他解释了这一点。 “看，疯狂帮的事情已经结束了。你是最好的球员之一。你必须带着责任感去打球。你是队长。作为队长，你是其他人的榜样。我希望你能以一种非常适合你的方式打球：控球，始终控球，尝试与前锋建立联系。如果你踢得好，我保证你也会在国家队踢球。”人们普遍认为霍德尔在 90 年代早期的影响力开启了我们今天所知的现代切尔西，但古利特确实做出了一些根本性的改变，可以说，最重要的是改变了球员的日常工作。他们在训练间隙在俱乐部的哈灵顿训练场一起吃饭，鼓励他们谈论足球，从而培养对比赛的自主感。古利特不想采取家长式作风，而是一种以信任和自我管理为中心的方法。这也是他接任后解雇俱乐部营养师的原因之一。古利特：我只是想让他们考虑自己的比赛，同时也考虑球队。我想知道他们在想什么。我不想要任何机器人。机器人帮不了我。在球场上，情况会发生变化，所以当情况发生变化时，我需要能够在球场上承担责任的球员。古利特的方法得到了回报，特别是在斯坦福桥，球队整个赛季只输了两次，而11月份客场战胜老特拉福德证明了蓝军可以将其与当天最好的球队结合起来。亚历克斯·弗格森表示，在曼联那个赛季面对的所有球队中，切尔西“在进攻三区的想象力最为丰富”。 古力特：我见过令人难以置信的比赛。 当然，利物浦（足总杯）是最好的例子，但我喜欢看他们的比赛。这就是为什么我更加退缩自己，看看自己需要改进什么，需要做什么。克拉克：参加比赛感觉很棒，我们踢了一些很棒的足球、传球和跑动。玩得很自由。玩得毫无畏惧。对于俱乐部和球队来说，这是一个真正美好时期的开始。我现在仍然和很多支持者交谈，他们谈论那段时间，格伦统治的结束和路德古利特统治的开始，这是切尔西近年来踢出的最好的足球。与那个团队联系在一起并以这种方式被铭记真是太好了。尼尔森：我认为对于切尔西球迷来说，我可以为自己说话，感觉我们终于来到了聚会。我想如果你对我们的处境很诚实的话，我们是伦敦的第三支球队。我们一直在争夺伦敦的第三名。毫无疑问，阿森纳已经孤军奋战了。托特纳姆热刺，只是因为他们在61年什么时候获得了双冠王？他们赢得了几个奖杯，所以他们仍然比我们赢得更多。我们真的是第三名。那很痛。现在的心情是我们这里有一些特别的东西。我们没有像克里·迪克森这样的零星优秀前锋，也没有雷·威尔金斯在中场，也没有零星的伟大进球。不，我们有一个团队。这很令人兴奋。这不仅仅是因为我们有一个团队。这是足球的品牌。我们正在踢中立者想要观看的足球，这对切尔西来说是一个相当大的赞美。这是一段恋情，是与这支全新国际球队真正恋情的开始，因为我认为是在 90 年代中期，我们才真正成为一家国际俱乐部。我喜欢那个团队。他们让切尔西重新焕发了自信。国王路、富勒姆路，我们最后一次拥有这样的赃物是在 70 年代初，艾伦·哈德森、奥西·彼得·奥斯古德、查理·库克和伊恩·哈钦森。中间有20年的差距，然后我们又恢复了自信。在重述 1996/97 赛季故事的第二篇长读中，我们将在马修·哈丁不幸去世 30 周年之际缅怀他……

news.title: Ultimate Goal of the Season: Semi-final results
news.title_zh: 本赛季终极目标：半决赛结果
news.body_en: Michael Essien will face Eden Hazard in the final of our Ultimate Goal of the Season competition. It is fitting that two of the three players (the other being Ramires) who have won the Chelsea Goal of the Season award more than once have made it to the very end. Essien's thunderbolt against Arsenal - the maiden winner of the Goal of the Season award in 2007 - edged past Ramires' chip in the Nou Camp with a 58 per cent share of the vote. In the other semi-final, Hazard's solo effort against Arsenal beat Moises Caicedo's halfway line lob with an 82 per cent share of the vote. Now, both the goals scored against Arsenal will compete to be crowned Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season when the voting opens on Monday!
news.body_zh: 迈克尔·埃辛将在我们赛季终极进球竞赛的决赛中对阵艾登·阿扎尔。多次获得切尔西赛季最佳进球奖的三名球员中，有两人（另一名是拉米雷斯）走到了最后，这是很合适的。埃辛对阵阿森纳时的雷霆万钧——2007年首次获得赛季最佳进球奖——在诺坎普球场以58%的得票率击败了拉米雷斯。在另一场半决赛中，阿扎尔对阵阿森纳时的个人射门以82%的得票率击败了莫伊塞斯·凯塞多的中线吊射。现在，对阵阿森纳的两个进球将在周一投票开始时角逐切尔西赛季最佳进球！

news.title: Internationals: Martinez and Barco feature in Argentina rout
news.title_zh: 国际比赛：马丁内斯和巴科在阿根廷大败中发挥作用
news.body_en: Emiliano Martinez and Valentin Barco represented Argentina on Saturday night as they thrashed Burkina Faso 7-0 in Buenos Aires. Martinez started in goal for Lionel Scaloni’s side as they made light work of the African outfit, who only arrived five hours before kick-off and were missing several senior players who opted not to travel. Argentina led 5-0 at half-time courtesy of goals from Lautaro Martinez, Gianluca Prestianni, Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and an own goal. Our goalkeeper was a virtual spectator. Barco came off the bench midway through the second half, by which point Franco Mastantuono had extended Argentina’s lead and Martinez held the captain's armband. Martinez was withdrawn with 12 minutes remaining and then Barco had a telling impact, assisting Giuliano Simeone’s header that made it 7-0 with a perfectly weighted far-post cross. Argentina’s third and final friendly of this international window is against Benin on Tuesday, a game which will make the formal end of Lionel Messi’s 21-year international career.
news.body_zh: 周六晚上，埃米利亚诺·马丁内斯和瓦伦丁·巴尔科代表阿根廷队在布宜诺斯艾利斯以 7-0 击败布基纳法索。马丁内斯为莱昂内尔·斯卡洛尼的球队首发门将，球队在开赛前五个小时才抵达非洲球队，并且错过了几名选择不前往的高级球员。半场结束时，凭借劳塔罗·马丁内斯、吉安卢卡·普雷斯蒂亚尼、尼科·帕斯、朱利安·阿尔瓦雷斯的进球和乌龙球，阿根廷队以 5-0 领先。我们的守门员是一个虚拟观众。下半场中段，巴科替补登场，弗兰科·马斯坦托诺扩大了阿根廷队的领先优势，马丁内斯则戴上了队长袖标。比赛还剩 12 分钟时，马丁内斯被换下场，随后巴科发挥了重要作用，助攻朱利亚诺·西蒙尼 (Giuliano Simeone) 头球攻门，完美的远门柱传中将比分改写为 7-0。阿根廷队本次国际比赛窗口期的第三场也是最后一场友谊赛将于周二对阵贝宁，这场比赛将正式结束梅西 21 年的国家队生涯。

news.title: Chelsea loan report: Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen and Harrison shine
news.title_zh: 切尔西租借报告：沃尔什、卡武玛-麦奎因和哈里森大放异彩
news.body_en: We delve into how the Chelsea players out on loan fared in September, with Reggie Walsh, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Ollie Harrison catching the eye… Walsh has featured in every Wigan match since joining the League One club on loan and has continued to impress with his maturity in the heart of midfield, despite being the second-youngest player in the division so far this season. The England Under-19 international (pictured top, photo credit: Bernard Platt) started five of the Latics’ six matches during September and was brought on at half-time in the other. Kavuma-McQueen is the youngest player in the Championship to have made over 120 minutes this season. He made an impact from the bench in games against Bristol City and Derby County before being restored to Pompey’s starting XI for their final fixture of the month. He made the most of the opportunity, providing an assist in the 74th minute as Portsmouth came from behind to earn a 2-2 draw against Blackburn. Harrison enjoyed an excellent month at Wimbledon, helping his side go unbeaten in their final four matches of September. The midfielder has been a key part of that impressive run, helping the Dons keep three clean sheets and concede just once across 360 minutes of football. Since being named in the team that beat Bromley, Harrison has established himself as a regular in the side, making four consecutive starts. Richards made his Wimbledon debut from the bench in the goalless draw with MK Dons and impressed enough to earn a first start against Cambridge the following week. Wilson has made a fine start to life at Rochdale, featuring in six matches during September. He played 627 league minutes during the month, the most of any of the Academy loanees. The defender helped his side keep three clean sheets during that run, with his defensive discipline from left-back helping Rochdale's form improve as they have climbed the League Two table. Genesis Antwi and Filip Jorgensen have established themselves as regulars for Strasbourg, with both players completing the full 90 minutes in all three of the French side's Ligue 1 matches during September, the highlight of which was a thrilling 6-2 victory against Troyes. Having only turned 19 in May, Antwi is the third-youngest player in Ligue 1 to have played more than 400 minutes this season. Dario Essugo made three substitute appearances during September, registering an assist in that big win over Troyes. Mhueka made five substitute appearances for Celtic in September, helping the Bhoys record victories in each of his first three appearances before successive defeats to rivals Rangers. Wiley scored his first goal of the season during September, netting Preston's only goal in a 3-1 defeat to Bristol City. The full-back was handed another start in his next outing and helped his side claim a 2-1 victory over Blackburn Rovers. Dyer was handed two starts in the EFL Trophy and made four substitute appearances in League Two during September. The midfielder produced an impressive assist in their EFL Trophy clash with Port Vale, helping the tie finish level and go to penalties, where Chesterfield eventually prevailed. Samuels-Smith made two appearances for Notts County in September, one from the bench before being handed a start in their final game of the month. The defender acquitted himself well in the 2-1 victory over Grimsby Town, operating in a left wing-back role as the Magpies secured all three points. Satpayev started Burnley's 1-1 draw with Middlesbrough at the beginning of September, playing 81 minutes for the Clarets before being forced off with an injury. The young goalkeeper picked up a thigh problem during Hartlepool’s game against Woking at the start of September which has kept him sidelined since. Sarr made three starts for Real Sociedad during September, beginning with an impressive debut against Elche. The defender helped his side to a 3-2 away victory before putting in another solid display against Atletico Madrid. Sarr also played the full 90 minutes in Sociedad's Europa League meeting with Bournemouth, although they suffered a 2-1 defeat. Disasi featured in four matches across three competitions for Crystal Palace during September, keeping two clean sheets in the process and impressing during their Europa League meeting with Lech Poznan. The centre-back was then shown a first-half red card as Palace fell to defeat against Ipswich Town in the Premier League. He subsequently missed their next fixture through suspension and will remain unavailable for their next two league matches. Badiashile was a late substitute as Napoli fell to a 3-2 defeat against reigning champions Inter Milan at the San Siro. Garnacho made one appearance for Aston Villa in September, coming off the bench for the final 15 minutes as they drew 0-0 with Hull City. Mudryk made a late appearance from the bench as Tottenham played out a goalless Premier League draw with Nottingham Forest. The attacker has otherwise been absent for our London rivals after picking up an ankle injury in training. Sanchez made his Como debut in Serie A against Parma, helping Cesc Fabregas's side to a 2-1 victory. We will bring you the latest on how all our loanees are faring at the end of every month on the Chelsea Official App and website.

news.title: Internationals: Rogers provides gloss on historic England win
news.title_zh: 国际比赛：罗杰斯为英格兰队的历史性胜利锦上添花
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers scored the final goal as England stunned Croatia by inflicting their heaviest defeat on record, as the Three Lions ran out 7-0 winners in Rijeka. The unforgettable win also means England have equalled the record for the biggest margin of victory in the Nations League since the competition was launched in 2018, matching Germany's 7–0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in November 2024. Croatia went into the contest 13th in the world rankings but you wouldn't have thought there were only nine places between the sides as England dominated from start to finish. Having started Tuesday’s victory over Czechia, Rogers was among the substitutes for this encounter as former Chelsea head coach Thomas Tuchel made five changes to his starting XI. England took control early on, with Harry Kane opening the scoring after eight minutes following a pass from Bellingham. The midfielder then added his own name to the scoresheet, before Anthony Gordon headed home Jarell Quansah’s delivery and Bukayo Saka made it four before the interval. There was little respite for the hosts after the restart. Kane converted Elliot Anderson’s low cross to register his second of the evening, before turning provider for Saka to complete his own double midway through the half. Rogers entered the action in the 69th minute and soon threatened to create another, finding Saka with a low ball from the left, only for the winger to fire over. Our No.10 would have a goal to celebrate himself with three minutes of normal time remaining, though. Rogers timed his run in behind perfectly as Bellingham released the 24-year-old. He then showed composure to take it around goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic before finishing into the unguarded net. The Three Lions conclude their extended international break back at Wembley on Tuesday against Czechia. As England's senior team were dismantling Croatia, their Under-20s were on the way to lifting the La Nucia International U20 Tournament. Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka, who is currently on loan at Celtic, made it two goals in two starts for England Under-20s as he scored the opener against Germany after 38 minutes, latching onto a through ball to slot into the bottom corner from around 15 yards out. The England Under-20s side also included Jesse Derry, who is on loan at Sporting CP, and went down to ten men in first-half injury-time when Jack Fletcher was sent off. However, the Young Lions still took a 2-0 lead just after half-time when Kian Noble fired in from close range when Germany failed to clear a corner. Eric da Silva Moreira pulled a goal back for Germany Under-20s with 12 minutes remaining but England finished the tournament unbeaten after victories over Italy (3-1) and France (2-1). It was to be defeat for our England Under-18s players, though, as they lost 2-0 to Spain in the final of the UEFA Friendship Cup. Chelsea's Calvin Diakite, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Jashayde Greenwood all started the match, with Gabriel Sambou also on the bench. Greenwood shot over early on and hit the post late in the game, while Kavuma-McQueen went close to scoring on a few occasions in the first half, but in the end, Spain were victorious thanks to Junior's finish just before half-time and Rafa Cruz's goal in the seventh minute of injury-time.
news.body_zh: 摩根·罗杰斯打入最后一球，英格兰队在里耶卡以 7-0 的比分击败了克罗地亚队，遭遇了历史上最惨重的失利。这场令人难忘的胜利也意味着英格兰追平了自2018年这项赛事启动以来，欧洲国家联赛中最大的胜利纪录，追平了德国在2024年11月以7-0战胜波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那的成绩。克罗地亚在世界排名中排名第13位，但你不会想到英格兰从始至终都占据主导地位，双方之间只有9个名次。在周二战胜捷克队的比赛中，罗杰斯首发出场，他是这场比赛的替补球员之一，前切尔西主教练托马斯·图赫尔对首发阵容进行了五次调整。英格兰队一开始就控制了比赛，八分钟后哈里·凯恩接贝林厄姆的传球首开纪录。这位中场球员随后将自己的名字写入了进球表，随后安东尼·戈登接贾雷尔·夸萨的传球头球破门，布卡约·萨卡在中场休息前将比分扳为四分。重启后，主队几乎没有喘息的机会。凯恩将埃利奥特·安德森的低传中转化为他当晚的第二个传中，然后在半场中段为萨卡完成了自己的双杀。罗杰斯在第69分钟介入，很快又制造了一次威胁，他从左路低传给萨卡，但边锋的射门高出。不过，我们的 10 号球员将在比赛还剩三分钟时进球庆祝自己。罗杰斯完美地追赶了他，贝林汉姆释放了这位 24 岁的球员。然后他表现出镇静，将球绕过门将多米尼克·利瓦科维奇，然后射入无人防守的球网。三狮军团周二在温布利对阵捷克队的比赛中结束了漫长的国际比赛。当英格兰成年队击败克罗地亚队时，他们的 20 岁以下青年队也即将夺得拉努西亚国际 U20 锦标赛的冠军。目前租借到凯尔特人队的切尔西前锋希姆·穆卡 (Shim Mheuka) 在英格兰 20 岁以下国家队的两场首发中攻入两球，他在第 38 分钟对阵德国队的比赛中攻入首球，他在 15 码外接到直塞球入球底角。这支英格兰20岁以下青年队还包括租借到里斯本竞技队的杰西·德里(Jesse Derry)，在上半场伤停补时阶段，杰克·弗莱彻(Jack Fletcher)被罚下场后，他的出场人数减少到了10人。然而，上半场刚结束，德国队未能解​​出角球，基安·诺布尔近距离射门，幼狮队仍以2-0领先。埃里克·达·席尔瓦·莫雷拉 (Eric da Silva Moreira) 在比赛还剩 12 分钟时为德国 20 岁以下青年队扳回一球，但英格兰队在战胜意大利 (3-1) 和法国 (2-1) 后保持不败。不过，这对我们的英格兰U-18球员来说却是一场失败，因为他们在欧洲联盟友谊杯决赛中以2-0输给了西班牙。切尔西队的卡尔文·迪亚基特、瑞安·卡武马·麦奎因和贾沙伊德·格林伍德均首发出场，加布里埃尔·桑布也坐在替补席上。格林伍德在比赛后期的射门高出，并在比赛后期击中门柱，而卡武马-麦奎因在上半场几次差点进球，但最终，西班牙凭借儒尼奥尔在半场结束前的射门和拉法·克鲁兹在伤停补时第7分钟的进球取得了胜利。

news.title: Internationals: Estevao continues impressive Brazil form
news.title_zh: 国际比赛：埃斯特沃继续在巴西表现出色
news.body_en: Estevao showed his class for Brazil as the Chelsea man scored and assisted during their 4-0 win over India. The forward missed this summer's World Cup due to injury but has since featured in all three of Selecao's matches, starting against Australia eight days ago and again tonight. His goal and assist on Saturday mean it is now six goals in nine games for Brazil since his move to Chelsea in the summer of 2025. The 19-year-old had the first chance of the match when he shot wide after just two minutes, and Marquinhos then headed wide from Estevao's corner soon after. The Chelsea man eventually broke the deadlock just before the half-hour mark when he showed good skill to drive inside from the right touchline, before cutting onto his left foot just inside the penalty area and his low shot towards the near post was too powerful for the goalkeeper. It was more good work from Estevao which led to Brazil's second goal just before the break, as he picked out the run of Flamengo striker Pedro and once again his strike was too powerful for the India goalkeeper to stop. A good finish from Samuel Lino made it 3-0 a quarter of an hour after the restart, before Estevao made way on 67 minutes. Brazil then wrapped up the win and their extended international window deep into stoppage time when Samuel smashed in a fourth.
news.body_zh: 埃斯特沃在巴西队 4-0 战胜印度队的比赛中进球并助攻，展现了他在巴西队的出色表现。这位前锋因伤缺席了今年夏天的世界杯，但此后参加了桑巴军团的全部三场比赛，八天前对阵澳大利亚的比赛首发，今晚再次出场。他在周六的进球和助攻意味着自 2025 年夏天转会切尔西以来，巴西队在 9 场比赛中打进了 6 个进球。这位 19 岁的球员在仅仅两分钟后就获得了比赛的第一次机会，他的射门偏出，不久之后，马尔基尼奥斯从埃斯特沃的角球中头球攻门偏出。这位切尔西球员最终在半小时前打破了僵局，他展示了出色的技术，从右侧边线内切入内线，然后在禁区内左脚切入，他的低射近门柱对门将来说太强大了。埃斯特沃的表现更加出色，在中场休息前为巴西队打进了第二个进球，他挑出了弗拉门戈前锋佩德罗的跑动，他的射门再次威力强大，让印度门将无法阻止。比赛重新开始一刻钟后，塞缪尔·利诺 (Samuel Lino) 的精彩射门将比分改写为 3-0，随后埃斯特瓦奥 (Estevao) 在第 67 分钟破门。随后，萨穆埃尔打进第四球，巴西队在伤停补时阶段结束了胜利，并延长了国际比赛窗口期。
